definition.en-US: An AI coding assistant is a program that reads your project files, makes the changes you ask for, and reports back in plain language.

analogy.en-US: It is like a helper who can open your filing cabinet, edit the papers you point to, and tell you exactly what they changed.

definition.en-US: Usage-based billing charges you for the amount of text a model reads and writes, measured in tokens, rather than a fixed monthly fee.

analogy.en-US: It is like a taxi meter, where you pay for the distance you actually travel instead of one flat fare.

definition.en-US: An API key is a secret string that identifies your account to a service so the service can serve your requests and bill you for them.

analogy.en-US: It is like a hotel key card that opens your room and is tied to your bill.

definition.en-US: A brief is a short written request that tells an assistant what to build, why, and how you will know it is done.

analogy.en-US: It is like the order form you hand a carpenter before any wood is cut, so you both picture the same table.

definition.en-US: A done checklist is a list of things you can check by looking or clicking, which you write before the work starts.

analogy.en-US: It is like the list you tick through before a trip, checking the passport and tickets one by one.

definition.en-US: A local preview is your site opened in your own browser from files on your computer, before anyone else can see it.

analogy.en-US: It is like trying on a jacket in the mirror at home before you buy it.

definition.en-US: A checkpoint is a saved state of the files and conversation that an assistant can return to later.

analogy.en-US: It is like a bookmark in a long book that lets you flip back to a page you know was good.

definition.en-US: A commit is a saved snapshot of your project's files with a short message that describes the change.

analogy.en-US: It is like a save point in a video game that you can load if the next level goes wrong.

definition.en-US: A diff is a view of what changed between two versions of a file, showing the lines that were added and removed.

analogy.en-US: It is like comparing two drafts of an essay, with every new sentence marked in one colour and every deleted one struck through.

definition.en-US: A rollback returns your files to an earlier saved state that you know worked.

analogy.en-US: It is like tearing out the pages you wrote after the last good draft and starting again from that draft.

definition.en-US: A self-review is an assistant's own report on whether its work matches the request, which you should treat as a second opinion.

analogy.en-US: It is like a student marking their own exam, which is useful but does not replace the teacher's grading.

definition.en-US: An acceptance check is a test you run yourself, with a fixed input and an expected output, to decide that the work is finished.

analogy.en-US: It is like a building inspector who walks through the finished house with the plans in hand before signing it off.

definition.en-US: A permission mode is the setting that decides which actions an assistant may take without asking you first.

analogy.en-US: It is like a family rule about which errands a child may run alone and which need a phone call first.

definition.en-US: A secret is any value, such as a password or an API key, that lets someone act as you or spend your money.

analogy.en-US: It is like a spare key under the doormat, because anyone who finds it can walk in.
